The appellant has filed this criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 being aggrieved by order dated 11.03.2025 passed by the Special Judge, (SC/ST Act), Shivpuri, whereby bail application u/S 439 of Cr.P.C. of appellant has been rejected.

sentences.text: 3. The appellant has been arrested on 21.02.2025 relating to Crime No.192 of 2019 registered at Police Station Karera District Shivpuri (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 376, 366, 506 of IPC and Sections 3(2) (va), 3(1)(w)(ii) of the SC/ST Act.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:8192 2 CRA-3533-2025 4.
This is a case of bail jump.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that earlier, the appellant was granted bail by the Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 26.07.2019 passed in Cr.A. No.5935/2019.
Thereafter, during trial, he remained absent before the Trial Court on 28.02.2020 and thereafter, he has been arrested on 21.02.2025.
Earlier, the appellant was granted bail with the condition that he shall plant 2 saplings (either fruit bearing trees or Neem/Peepal) and thereafter will nurture them.

It is submitted that though appellant has planted the trees as directed by the Court but since he Kamal Singh Pal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92010111/

sentences.text: The appellant had gone out of station to earn his livelihood, and therefore, could not appear before the Trial Court.
As regards criminal antecedents, one more case was registered against the appellant which is related to year 2012 and might have been disposed of.
He is ready and willing to abide by any condition which may be imposed by the Court.
Appellant further undertakes to cooperate in trial and would make himself available as and when required by the trial Court and to do some community service.
The trial will take time to conclude.
On these grounds, learned counsel for the appellant prays that the impugned order be set-aside and appellant may be extended benefit of bail.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the appeal and prays for its rejection.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
8.

Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and the facts and circumstances of the case, while setting aside the order dated NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:8192 3 CRA-3533-2025 11.03.2025 passed by the Trial Court, this Court is inclined to release the appellant on bail.

Thus, without commenting on the merits of the case, the appeal is allowed and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court/Committal Court.

As per the undertaking given by counsel on behalf of the appellant, it is hereby directed that appellant shall plant 5 saplings (fruit bearing trees) alongwith tree guards or has to make Kamal Singh Pal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92010111/
2 arrangement for fencing for protection of the trees because it is the duty of the appellant not only to plant the saplings but also to nurture them.

sentences.text: He shall plant saplings/ trees preferably of 6-8 ft., so that they would grow into full fledged trees at an early time.

For ensuring the compliance, he shall have to submit all the photographs of plantation of trees/ saplings before the concerned trial Court alongwith a report within 30 days from the date of release of the appellant.
The report shall be submitted by the appellant before the trial Court every month till conclusion of the trial.

It is the duty of the trial Court to monitor the progress of the trees because human existence is at stake because of the environmental degradation and Court cannot put a blind fold over any casualness shown by the appellant regarding compliance.

Therefore, trial Court is directed to submit a report regarding progress of the trees and the compliance made by the appellant by placing a short report before this Court every quarterly (every three months), which shall be placed under the caption "Direction" before this Court.
Any default on behalf of appellant in plantation or caring of trees shall disentitle the appellant from enjoying the benefit of bail.

The appellant shall be at liberty to plant these saplings/trees at an place of his choice if he intends to protect the trees on his own cost by providing tree guards or fencing.
10.
The Trial Court will be at liberty to forfeit the amount of earlier bail bonds.

A copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned Certified copy as per rules.
